paper_b.title: Noise-Contrastive Estimation: A New Estimation Principle for Unnormalized Statistical Models

metadata.description: Both papers use the same core technique: train a logistic-regression classifier to distinguish samples of a target distribution from samples of a contrastive distribution, and the optimal discriminator has the form p_target/(p_target+p_contrast). NCE (2010) introduces this as a parameter-estimation principle for unnormalized statistical models with a fixed noise distribution p_n. GAN (2014) reuses the same discriminator-as-density-ratio principle but learns the contrastive distribution as a generator G(z), turning it into an adversarial minimax game for implicit generative modeling. Hence SM (same method, different problems): the classifier-against-noise machinery is shared, while the problems (density estimation up to normalization vs implicit sampler training) and the noise role (fixed vs learned) differ. NCE paper is PDF-fallback so we lean on names and types over exact LaTeX in matches.

matches.explanation: Both are the top-level optimization problem the paper sets out to solve, and both reduce to maximizing an expected logistic-classification objective between data and a contrastive distribution. They are analogous rather than exact because NCE's problem is parametric estimation of an unnormalized density p_m(x;alpha) with intractable Z(alpha), whereas GAN's problem is finding an implicit generator G whose induced distribution p_g matches p_data. The shared structure (same minimax/classification objective) is what motivates the SM tag for the pair.

Both nodes define the parametric family being fit to data. In GAN the generator G(z;theta_g) implicitly defines a density p_g; in NCE the unnormalized model p_m^0(.;alpha) with explicit log-normalization parameter c defines an explicit (up to that scalar) density p_m. The match is loose because the parametrizations are radically different (implicit pushforward of noise vs explicit unnormalized density with learned partition function), but they occupy the same role in their respective frameworks: the model whose parameters the procedure outputs.

Same mathematical object: a logistic classifier whose output is the posterior probability that an input came from one distribution rather than another. GAN's discriminator D(x;theta_d) outputs the probability that x is from p_data versus p_g; NCE's h(u;theta) = sigma(ln p_m(u) - ln p_n(u)) and EP213.2's identity P(C=1|u) = p_m/(p_m+p_n) are precisely the same construct with p_n in place of p_g. The two NCE equation nodes together (definition of h and the explicit posterior form) cover what the single GAN definition node states.

Same objective up to an overall factor and the identity of the contrastive distribution. GAN's V(D,G) = E_{p_data}[log D(x)] + E_{p_g}[log(1-D(G(z)))] and NCE's J_T(theta) = (1/2T) sum_t [log h(x_t;theta) + log(1 - h(y_t;theta))] are both the binary-cross-entropy log-likelihood for logistic discrimination of data against noise/generator samples. The GAN value-function definition (DP212.3) and the explicit minimax equation (EP212.1) jointly state on the GAN side what DP213.2 states on the NCE side.

Both are the population-level (or after-D-optimization) version of the contrastive objective viewed as a functional. GAN's C(G) = max_D V(G,D) is the value function after the discriminator has been optimized away; NCE's tilde{J}(f) is the population objective viewed as a functional of f = ln p_m. Analogous because GAN's elimination is a max over the discriminator class while NCE's J(theta)/tilde{J}(f) is the infinite-sample limit of the empirical objective; the resulting object plays the same role (a functional whose optimizer characterizes the desired distribution).

Identical closed-form: D*_G(x) = p_data(x) / (p_data(x) + p_g(x)) is exactly NCE's posterior P(C=1|u;theta) = p_m(u;theta) / (p_m(u;theta) + p_n(u)) under the substitution (p_data, p_g) <-> (p_m, p_n). GAN's proposition (PrP212.1) and equation (EP212.2) jointly establish the result; NCE states it as the equation EP213.2 used to motivate the J_T construction.

Both theorems characterize the unique global optimum of the population-level contrastive objective and identify it with the data distribution. GAN's TP212.1 says C(G) is minimized iff p_g = p_data (with min value -log 4) in the nonparametric setting. NCE's TP213.1 says tilde{J}(f) is maximized at f = ln p_d with no other extrema. Both are nonparametric / capacity-unconstrained statements; both rely on a positivity-of-support assumption (NCE explicit; GAN implicit via 'enough capacity'); the underlying convex-analysis argument is the same. Analogous (not exact) because the GAN proof routes through Jensen-Shannon divergence while NCE's argument is a direct functional-derivative analysis.

Both establish that the empirical/iterative procedure converges to the truth. GAN's PrP212.2 proves p_g converges to p_data under sufficient capacity, optimal D at each step, and small enough updates -- a population/algorithmic convergence statement. NCE's TP213.2 proves consistency hat{theta}_T -> theta^* under positivity of p_n, uniform convergence of J_T to J, and full-rank of the noise-weighted information matrix I. Analogous because both are the 'the procedure works' theorem of their respective papers, but the GAN result is about the iterative subgradient dynamics on p_g while NCE's is the standard M-estimator consistency for the maximizer of J_T.

Both are the paper's main training algorithm: gradient-based maximization of the noise/adversary-contrastive log-likelihood over the model parameters. NCE's AP213.1 maximizes J_T(theta) over (alpha, c) with a generic gradient optimizer (e.g. conjugate gradient) and a fixed pre-sampled noise set Y. GAN's AP212.1 alternates k inner SGD ascent steps on theta_d (the discriminator) with one SGD descent step on theta_g (the generator); the noise/generator distribution itself is learned. Analogous (not exact) because GAN has the additional outer loop over the generator and re-samples noise via G(z) at every step, whereas NCE optimizes a single objective with fixed noise. The matched algorithm_step children differ in the same way and are intentionally not aligned individually (per Level-2 rules).

Both remarks make the same observation: the contrastive objective IS the log-likelihood of logistic regression / Bayes-optimal classification of samples into two classes (data vs noise/generator) with equal class priors. GAN's RP212.2 phrases it as 'D's objective is the conditional log-likelihood for P(Y=y|x)' with Y=1 iff x ~ p_data; NCE's RP213.1 phrases it as 'J_T equals (up to a constant factor) the log-likelihood of logistic regression discriminating X from Y'. This is the conceptual bridge that makes the two papers methodologically the same.
GAN-specific algebraic step: rewriting C(G) as -log 4 + KL(p_data || (p_data+p_g)/2) + KL(p_g || (p_data+p_g)/2). No NCE counterpart -- NCE never reformulates J as a sum of KL divergences.
GAN-specific algebraic step: C(G) = -log 4 + 2 JSD(p_data || p_g). NCE has no analogous JSD identity; its information-geometric quantity is I, not a divergence between p_d and p_n.

GAN's pointwise-maximization proof of the optimal discriminator. NCE writes down the analogous closed form (EP213.2) directly without an explicit proof node, so PP212.1 has no proof counterpart in the NCE JSON. (The analogous closed-form result IS matched at the EP212.2 / PrP212.1 <-> EP213.2 entry above.)

GAN's proof of global optimality routes through JSD non-negativity. NCE's proof of TP213.1 (which IS aligned at the theorem level) is a direct functional-calculus argument and is not extracted as a separate proof node in the NCE JSON; even if it were, the proof techniques are different enough that this is a clean none on the proof-as-an-object level.

GAN's proof of convergence of the adversarial training procedure (subgradient argument on the convex envelope sup_D U(p_g, D)). NCE has no proof-typed counterpart in the JSON for its consistency theorem TP213.2.

Definition of the NCE estimator as the argmax of J_T. GAN has no analogous named definition node for 'the trained parameters' as a distinct mathematical object -- the trained (theta_g, theta_d) are simply the output of the AP212.1 algorithm, never elevated to a definition. Hence none on the definition-as-an-object level, even though the matched algorithms produce conceptually similar objects.

NCE-specific construction: the noise-weighted matrix I = integral g(x) g(x)^T P(x) p_d(x) dx that controls consistency and asymptotic variance. GAN has no analogous information-geometric quantity -- its asymptotic theory is replaced by a (much weaker) population-level convergence claim.

NCE's asymptotic-normality theorem with explicit covariance Sigma. GAN provides no analogous CLT-style result for the trained parameters -- there is no asymptotic-distribution analysis in the GAN paper at all.
NCE's MSE-rate corollary (MSE ~ tr(Sigma)/T). GAN does not derive any finite-sample or MSE rate for its estimator; this is a parameter-estimation perspective NCE has and GAN lacks.
